title: [M1][M2] Jump key skips the sessions that are actually blocked: permission prompts and AskUserQuestion never enter its queue (or only after ~92 s)
repro: Fleet: kestrel blocked on a Bash permission prompt (tool_use record not written while the dialog is up), beacon blocked on AskUserQuestion, vibepet done
Launch vibepet against the fleet root; press the jump key (registered handler or OS-level)
Re-prompt vibepet to a fresh done turn; press again
Let kestrel raise a permission prompt whose tool_use IS written; poll pending() until it appears
expected: The key walks what needs you, longest-blocked first: beacon (AskUserQuestion, blocked since 02:13:42.7) then kestrel (approval), then done sessions; a block enters the queue <=3 s after it starts.
actual: 02:24:16: queue empty, snapshot lists no sessions; 3 presses do nothing while kestrel is blocked 20.5 min and beacon 10.6 min. 02:30:29: the only target is vibepet (done); kestrel's new prompt (02:29:42.9) shows as running for 120 s, then is dropped; beacon is never in the queue in 37.5 min. A written permission prompt (02:50:25.974) enters as 'stalled' only at 02:51:57.764 (+91.8 s). Walks seen all run: [], [vibepet(done)], [kestrel(question)], [kestrel(stalled)]; beacon never reachable.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S7/timings.json F2 'permission prompt … → session in the jump queue' 91790 ms / never; 'AskUserQuestion … ' never
truth: kestrel: registry waiting (permission prompt) since 02:03:49, again 02:29:42.9 and 02:50:26.0; beacon: waiting (input needed) since 02:13:42.7 the whole run; vibepet: idle/done (end_turn 02:12:19, 02:30:04.49)

title: [M11] Jump key lands on no tmux pane and copies `claude --resume <id>` over the clipboard on every press
repro: Have any fleet session (tmux, no attached client) in the jump queue
Press the jump key (OS-level ⌥⌘J, or the registered handler)
Inspect the jump IPC result, clipboard writes (stubbed), and `tmux display -p -t vp-<member>:0.0 '#{session_attached} #{window_active} #{pane_active}'` before/after
expected: The session's tmux window/pane is selected and the terminal hosting it is focused (the registry carries the pane, e.g. vp-kestrel:@W.%P), or the pet says exactly where it is; the clipboard is never overwritten with a command that forks a live session.
actual: 7/7 recorded jumps returned {ok:false, cmd:'cd <repo> && claude --resume <id>'} with one clipboard write each (vibepet 02:28:33 ×2 instances, 02:30:29; kestrel 02:47:06, 02:47:13, 02:50:10, 02:52:0x). tmux panes unchanged (session_attached=0, same window/pane). Bubble: 'couldn't find its terminal — resume command copied' although the pane exists; pasting the command would start a second claude on the live conversation.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S7/timings.json F2 'OS key → jump attempt finished' median 202 ms n=4
truth: vibepet idle/done in tmux pane vp-vibepet:0.0; kestrel question at end of turn (02:46:18.98) then permission prompt (02:50:26.0) in vp-kestrel:0.0; both live claude processes

title: [M11][T2] Failed-jump feedback is invisible when the roster pill or Home is open (the promised in-row note is never rendered)
repro: Queue a session (kestrel question); rest the pointer on Net so the roster pill is open
Press the jump key; screenshot 1.5 s later
Open Home; press again; check what is drawn over the bubble
Hide Net, press the key (summon + jump); sample the bubble's computed display every 250 ms
expected: The failure is visible wherever the user is looking: a note in the pill row / Home row, or a bubble above the panel.
actual: Pill open: bubble suppressed by CSS (#roster:not(.hidden) ~ #bubble {display:none}) and no row note (renderer noteFor() has no caller) → shot 25 byte-identical to shot 24. Home open: bubble drawn behind the panel (elementFromPoint at its centre = the panel; ghost visible in shot 26). After a key summon the pill hides it for the first 1.78 s.
truth: question at end of turn since 02:46:18.98 (needs a reply); jump failed {ok:false}

title: A failed jump marks every done session seen, so they leave the jump queue unvisited
repro: With a fresh done session in the queue (vibepet, unseen), press the jump key (tmux: jump fails)
Read pending() right after; press again after >4 s
expected: Only a successful jump (or the user actually looking at that row) marks that one session seen; a failed jump leaves the queue as it was.
actual: Queue [vibepet(ready)] → press at 02:30:29 → jump {ok:false} → queue [] (jumpTo() calls markSeen() first, which marks ALL ready rows). The next press after the 4 s window has nothing to walk, though the user reached no terminal.
truth: done (end_turn 02:30:04.49), alive at its prompt in tmux

title: [M3][M6] Jump order uses `since` (first time this pet saw the phase, or the last mtime touch), not when the block started
repro: Let a session finish, wait >5 min, let its transcript mtime move without a new record (observed at 02:24:57 / 02:25:20 / 02:41:29.36)
Read pending()[].since and the Home label
Separately: queue a written permission prompt and compare since with the tool_use timestamp
expected: Queue age and 'oldest first' use the block's real start (tool_use / end_turn timestamp, registry statusUpdatedAt).
actual: vibepet queued as done with since 02:24:57 and labelled 'done 1m ago' while done since 02:12:19 (12.6 min earlier); beacon reappeared as 'running 38s' after its 02:25:20 touch; kestrel's permission prompt queued with since 02:51:57.8 vs real start 02:50:26.0 (92 s); a relaunch restarts every since. Within a rank, 'oldest first' therefore sorts by the wrong clock.
truth: vibepet done since 02:12:19; beacon AskUserQuestion since 02:13:42.7; kestrel permission prompt since 02:50:26.0; transcript sizes unchanged across the mtime moves

title: [M15] A permission prompt is queued and shown as 'stuck' in red, ranking it below any question in the jump walk
repro: Let kestrel's permission prompt (tool_use written) age past 90 s
Look at Net and the Home row; read pending()
Have another session end its turn with a question: pending() sorts needs (question) before stuck (approval) regardless of age
expected: A permission prompt reads as waiting on you (e.g. 'needs approval · 1m 44s', amber) and ranks with questions by how long it has waited.
actual: Queued as phase 'stalled'; Net shows a red light and a red '?' (shot 29); Home row 'kestrel · stuck 1m' in red (shot 31). pending() sorts RANK needs > stuck before age, so a 30-min approval is walked after a question asked seconds ago (both phases observed on kestrel this run, 02:46 question → 'waiting', 02:51 approval → 'stalled'; not both at once).
truth: registry waiting (permission prompt) since 02:50:26.0, Bash ./deploy.sh --dry-run; nothing is stuck

title: Jump-key clash goes undetected: two apps register the same key, both report success, one press fires both
repro: Launch two pet instances (separate profiles) with the same jump key (⌥⌘J)
Check globalShortcut.isRegistered and keyTaken in both; open Settings → Jump key
Post OS-level presses of the key
expected: The second holder reports the key as taken ('Jump key (taken)' + offer the alternative); one press reaches one app.
actual: Both register() → true, keyTaken false, no '(taken)'. 4/4 OS presses fired both handlers within 1 ms (02:28:33, 02:44:28, 02:44:33, 02:44:38) and on the first press both also jumped and wrote the clipboard. Same for ⌃⌥⌘J: a test instance registered it with no '(taken)' while the user's installed pet with that saved key was running; ⌃⌥⌘R (record a short) also registered true alongside, so one ⌃⌥⌘R press would start a recording in both.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S7/timings.json F2 'OS key … → shortcut handler fires'
truth: two holders of ⌥⌘J, both instances of this app

title: Setup card's Keys row always says ⌃⌥⌘J, whatever the jump key is
repro: Settings → Jump key → ⌥⌘J (or Off)
⋯ → Setup…; read the Keys row
expected: The Keys row shows the active key (⌥⌘J), or 'Off' / 'taken'.
actual: '⌃⌥⌘J jump to who needs you · ⌃⌥⌘R record a short' while the saved and active jump key is ⌥⌘J (renderSetup hardcodes the text).

title: Dragging Net in a loop counts as the summon gesture and hides him
repro: Train a circle (Settings → Gesture → Record gesture…)
Press on Net's pixels, drag him around a closed (or 3/4) loop in ~0.9 s, release
expected: No toggle while a mouse button is held / while Net himself is being dragged.
actual: Loop drags hid Net 4/4 (two closed loops, one 0.85-turn, one 0.8-turn; ~198 ms after release; shots 20 → 21 → 22). The watcher samples only cursor position (gesture.js watcher), so any looping drag in any app (drawing, selecting) toggles too. Drags ending in a straight 140 px run did not (0/3).
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S7/timings.json F3 'loop drag of Net released → hide sent' 198 ms n=4

title: A square is recognized as the trained circle at the default Medium sensitivity
repro: Train a clockwise circle
Move the pointer in a 180 px square (clockwise, 0.8 s) near Net
Repeat at Settings → Gesture → Sensitivity → Low
expected: A square does not fire a circle gesture at the default setting.
actual: Medium: square fired 3/3 (hide, ~197 ms). Low: square 0/2, while circles 2/2 and a 2:1 ellipse 1/1 still fired — the default accepts a shape Low tells apart.

title: A counter-clockwise circle never matches a clockwise-trained circle, and nothing says direction matters
repro: Train a clockwise circle
Draw the same circle counter-clockwise (r=110, 0.6 s)
expected: Either closed loops match in both directions, or the pad tells the user to keep one direction.
actual: 0/3 matched; no feedback. Pad copy: 'A circle, a zig-zag or a “Z” works well'.

title: A summon gesture within 2.5 s of a hide is silently ignored
repro: Hide Net with the gesture
Draw it again to bring him back, ending ~1.3–1.7 s after the hide
expected: The reverse toggle is accepted, or the stroke is acknowledged.
actual: Strokes ending 1.35 s and 1.73 s after the hide: nothing, Net stays hidden, no feedback; one ending at 2.73 s summoned him.

title: Jump key gives no feedback when its queue is empty
repro: With nothing in the pet's queue (here: while two sessions are blocked but invisible to it), press the jump key
expected: A short acknowledgment (e.g. 'nobody's waiting on you') so a press is distinguishable from a dead key.
actual: 3 presses at 02:24: no bubble, no sound, no light change (shot 02) while kestrel was blocked 20.5 min and beacon 10.6 min.

title: 'Saved.' copy only says the shape brings Net back; the same shape also hides him
repro: Finish gesture training
Draw the shape while Net is visible
expected: Copy says the shape toggles Net (hides and brings back).
actual: 'Saved. Hide Net, then move the mouse in that shape to bring him back.' First use while visible hid him.

title: Jump failure bubble names the session by folder ('kestrel') while the pill and rows lead with its title ('Deploy.sh dry run')
repro: Press the jump key on a queued session whose title differs from its folder
expected: One consistent label (title + folder) across the bubble, pill and Home row.
actual: Bubble 'kestrel: couldn't find its terminal…' vs pill/row 'Deploy.sh dry run'.
